```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Regulatory exposure differs sharply. A's obligations are a security and data-retention posture, scoped as a one-time consult before enterprise pilots. B faces PCI scope, 1099-K reporting, sales tax/VAT, and an unresolved money-transmitter/KYC question. Its own brief says errors there create financial and legal exposure, which is a heavy load for one operator with agents inside 90 days.",
    "B's core value proposition is already beaten on price by its sourced competitors. Beamly charges 0% and Ko-fi charges 0–5%. B's own demand quotes show creators leaving Patreon for Ko-fi, an existing alternative, not asking for a new one.",
    "A has a clearer first paying customer: an eng team lead buying per-seat. Lody's sourced $8–10/seat price shows teams pay for the collaboration layer alone. B needs creators to accept switching costs, which its brief says historically required the founder to bring an owned audience.",
    "A's demand evidence describes a pain (invisible, unsteerable agent work) that two independent sources document. B's demand evidence is fee complaints that existing low-fee incumbents already address.",
    "Both are crowded. A's biggest threat is Slack Code, free and bundled into every Slack plan, which sets a $0 anchor. B's threat is worse: several cheap or free incumbents already own the 'Patreon alternative' search results, so B's main acquisition channel is effectively taken."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's only success precedent, the Starter Story founder who reached ~$140K MRR and exited for $3.5M, is a single anecdote. The brief itself says that result depended on an existing niche audience, which most solo builders lack on day one. So it supports B only under a condition the question's founder probably doesn't meet.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. A has serious gaps: its six-week buildability and its claim of demand beyond engineering are both marked [unsourced]. The YC RFS mention has no link, so it counts as missing. A also faces a free incumbent (Slack Code) and governance expectations (SOC2, SSO) that a solo build may not meet. Neither brief shows anyone paying a new entrant. A wins mainly because B carries heavier compliance risk and a value proposition its sourced competitors already undercut, not because A's evidence is strong."
}
```
